_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-09-13 16:36:24Z)**_

Found the issue. You added the full `.exe` path to your PATH instead of the **directory** containing it. PATH should contain the folder, not the file itself.

The user-level PATH has `C:\Users\vishc\Downloads\SpecStoryCLI_Windows_x86_64\specstory.exe` — but it needs to be `C:\Users\vishc\Downloads\SpecStoryCLI_Windows_x86_64`.

Also, keeping it in Downloads isn't ideal. I'd recommend moving the exe to a permanent location. Here's the fix:

**Option A — Fix in place (quick):** Update the PATH entry from the `.exe` path to just the directory. Run this in a new PowerShell terminal to fix it permanently:

```bash
$current = [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('PATH', 'User')
$fixed = $current -replace [regex]::Escape('C:\Users\vishc\Downloads\SpecStoryCLI_Windows_x86_64\specstory.exe'), 'C:\Users\vishc\Downloads\SpecStoryCLI_Windows_x86_64'
[System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('PATH', $fixed, 'User')
```

**Option B — Move to a proper location (recommended):** Put it somewhere permanent like `C:\Users\vishc\bin\`:

```bash
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "C:\Users\vishc\bin"
Copy-Item "C:\Users\vishc\Downloads\SpecStoryCLI_Windows_x86_64\specstory.exe" "C:\Users\vishc\bin\specstory.exe"
$current = [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('PATH', 'User')
[System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('PATH', "$current;C:\Users\vishc\bin", 'User')
```

After running either option, **open a new terminal** — PATH changes don't apply to already-open sessions. Then `specstory version` should work.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-09-13 16:54:46Z)**_

It's the **Claude Code Windows installer script** — a CMD (batch) bootstrap for environments where PowerShell isn't available.

What it does:
1. Takes an optional argument (`stable`, `latest`, or a specific version like `1.0.58`) — defaults to `latest`
2. Downloads the Claude Code binary from `downloads.claude.ai` using `curl`
3. Verifies the SHA256 checksum against a manifest
4. Runs `claude install` to set up the launcher and shell integration
5. Cleans up the temporary downloaded file

It's untracked (`??` in git status) — it was likely generated or downloaded as part of setting up Claude Code on this machine. You can safely ignore it or delete it since the installation is already done. It doesn't belong in the Gitea repo.

Launching with no interaction proves the entrypoint resolves. That's
not running the app - it's typechecking with extra steps. Drive it to

Go isn't installed at all, and `corepack enable` needs admin rights. You'll need to install these yourself — I can't run `winget` or `corepack` with the necessary permissions from here. Here's what to do:

---

**Step 1 — Install Go** (open a new terminal as yourself, not admin):

```bash
winget install GoLang.Go
```

Or download the installer from https://go.dev/dl/ and run it. After install, close and reopen your terminal.

---

**Step 2 — Install pnpm** (run this in a new terminal after Go is done):

```bash
npm install -g pnpm
```

(`corepack enable` needs admin; `npm install -g pnpm` does not.)

---

**Step 3 — Verify everything**:

```bash
go version
```

**Step 4 — Build and run Gitea** (from the repo root):

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm exec vite build

.\gitea.exe web
```

Then open **http://localhost:3000**, pick SQLite3, create an admin account, and click Install.

```text
# Gitea Testing Documentation Summary

Gitea employs four testing approaches: backend unit tests, integration tests, end-to-end tests, and migration tests. SQLite is the default local database, requiring no additional services.

## Test Types

**Unit Tests**: Backend tests exist in `*_test.go` files alongside their source code. Run all backend tests via `make test-backend` or individual tests using `go test -run '^TestName$'`. Frontend testing uses Vitest with commands like `make test-frontend`.

**Integration Tests**: Located in `tests/integration/`, these require Git LFS. The default SQLite database needs no external setup, though MySQL, PostgreSQL, and MSSQL are supported via environment variables and Docker containers.

**End-to-End Tests**: "End-to-end tests drive a running Gitea instance with Playwright." Run them using `make test-e2e` with optional environment variables for debugging and configuration.

**Migration Tests**: Required when modifying database-persisted structs. Execute via `make test-migration`.

## Key Commands

- `make test-backend` / `make test-frontend`
- `make test-integration`
- `make test-e2e`
- `make test-migration`

## CI Practice

The documentation emphasizes submitting pull requests with appropriate unit and integration tests, preferring unit tests for isolated logic and maintaining fast local test execution times under two seconds.
```
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-09-14 17:33:14Z)**_

Here's a summary of how to run tests in this repo:

---

## Running Tests

### Backend unit tests
```bash
make test-backend
```
Or a single test:
```bash
go test -run '^TestName$' ./path/to/package/
```

### Frontend unit tests
```bash
make test-frontend
```
Or a single file:
```bash
pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>
```

### Integration tests
```bash
make test-integration
```
Requires Git LFS. Defaults to SQLite — no extra setup needed.

### End-to-end tests (Playwright)
```bash
make test-e2e
```
Or a single file:
```bash
GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='<filepath>' make test-e2e
```

### Migration tests
```bash
make test-migration
```
Only needed if you modify database-persisted structs.

---

**Important caveats for Windows (from STUDENTS.md):** The test suite is validated on Linux CI. Run tests on **WSL2**, Linux, or macOS — not native Windows, where some unit tests fail due to symlink/temp-file differences unrelated to your code.

If you don't have `make`, the raw commands are:
- Backend: `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./...`
- Frontend: `pnpm exec vitest run`

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-09-14 20:06:31Z)**_

The problem is clear: **Go 1.27.1 is incompatible with the Go runtime source in WSL**. The errors (`unsafeTraceExpWriter redeclared`, `hashkey undefined`) are classic signs of a corrupted or mismatched Go installation — likely the 1.23.4 tarball was partially extracted first, and then 1.27.1 was overlaid on top, leaving mixed files.

Let me fix this by wiping `/usr/local/go` cleanly before re-extracting 1.27.1. Run this in your WSL terminal:

```bash
sudo rm -rf /usr/local/go && curl -fsSL https://go.dev/dl/go1.27.1.linux-amd64.tar.gz | sudo tar -C /usr/local -xz && go version
```

This removes the corrupted installation first, then extracts a clean 1.27.1. Once you see `go1.27.1 linux/amd64` come back, let me know and I'll re-run the tests.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-09-14 20:15:53Z)**_

Tests are running. Most packages pass. The failures are all the same root cause — **not real test failures**. They're caused by running the repo from a Windows NTFS path (`/mnt/c/...`) in WSL: git can't `chmod` `.gitconfig.lock` files on NTFS, which doesn't support Linux file permissions.

The fix is to clone the repo inside the WSL Linux filesystem instead. Run this in your WSL terminal:

```bash
git clone /mnt/c/Users/vishc/OneDrive/Documents/repos/gitea ~/gitea
```

Then run tests from there:

```bash
cd ~/gitea && CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./...
```

The `~/gitea` path lives on the native ext4 filesystem where `chmod` works properly. The real unit tests (models, services, etc.) are all passing — only the migration tests that need git config file locking are affected by the NTFS limitation.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-09-14 20:49:47Z)**_

Almost clean. Only **1 remaining failure** with Go 1.26.7:

**`gitea.dev/modules/git/pipeline` — `TestFindLFSFile`**

```
expected: 2022-12-21 17:56:42 -0500 EST
actual:   2022-12-21 17:56:42 -0500 -0500
```

This is a timezone name issue — WSL's Debian doesn't have the timezone database installed, so it can't resolve `EST` by name and falls back to the raw offset `-0500`. It's not a code bug. Fix it by running in your WSL terminal:


_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-09-14 20:59:49Z)**_

The issue is clear. `time.Parse` with `time.RFC3339` returns a `time.Location` with just the offset (`-0500`) and no named zone, while `stats[0].When` comes from git and gets resolved to the named timezone (`EST`) from the system tz database. They represent the same moment but `assert.Equal` considers them different because the `Location` pointer differs.

This is a pre-existing test fragility in the repo — it's environment-sensitive (timezone database presence/configuration). The test itself is the problem, not your code.

**Summary of final results:**
| | Result |
|---|---|
| **All models, services, routers, modules** | ✅ passing |
| `modules/json` | ✅ now passing (fixed by `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.7`) |
| `modules/git/pipeline` `TestFindLFSFile` | ❌ pre-existing timezone comparison bug in the test itself |
| **Frontend (vitest)** | ✅ 138/138 passing |

The `TestFindLFSFile` failure is a repo-level bug unrelated to anything you're working on — the test compares `time.Location` objects that are semantically equal but structurally different depending on whether the OS timezone database resolves named zones.

All failures have the same root cause: **`git lfs` is not installed**. Every failing test is an LFS-related test:

```

```

- `TestAPIGetRawFileOrLFS` — needs LFS
- `TestAPIGetRequestedFiles` — needs LFS
- `TestAPIGetContentsList` — needs LFS
- `TestAPIGetContents` — needs LFS
- `TestGitGeneral` — LFS subtests fail, rest pass
- `TestGitLFSSSH` — needs LFS

Install it in your WSL terminal:


_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-09-14 23:26:31Z)**_

Both failures have the same root cause: **timezone `time.Location` comparison**. The tests use `assert.Equal` on `time.Time` values, but `time.Parse` returns a location with no name (just an offset), while the actual value uses the system's `Local` timezone (which now has full zone data after installing tzdata).

The fix for both is to use `assert.True(t, tm.Equal(...))` instead of `assert.Equal` for time comparisons. Let me also check the integration test files:

Give me the commands to run the tests myself

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-09-15 00:01:35Z)**_

Here are the commands to run each test suite yourself in WSL:

**Backend unit tests**
```bash
cd ~/gitea && GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.7 make test-backend
```

**Frontend tests**
```bash
cd ~/gitea && pnpm exec vitest run
```

**Integration tests**
```bash
cd ~/gitea && GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.7 make test-integration
```

**E2E tests (full suite)**
```bash
cd ~/gitea && GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.7 make test-e2e
```

**E2E tests (single file)**
```bash
cd ~/gitea && GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='tests/e2e/pr-review.test.ts' GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.7 make test-e2e
```

**Single backend test**
```bash
cd ~/gitea && GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.7 go test -run '^TestName$' ./path/to/package/
```

**Before running — sync your Windows changes to WSL first:**
```bash
cd ~/gitea && git pull /mnt/c/Users/vishc/OneDrive/Documents/repos/gitea
```

And make sure your PATH has Go:
```bash
export PATH=/usr/local/go/bin:~/.npm-global/bin:$PATH
```

_**User (2026-09-15 16:00:38Z)**_

How do I start the WSL up again?

---

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-09-15 16:00:47Z)**_

Just open a new terminal and run:

```bash
wsl
```

That drops you into your Debian session. Then set up your PATH:

```bash
export PATH=/usr/local/go/bin:~/.npm-global/bin:$PATH
```

To make that permanent so you don't have to run it every time, add it to your `~/.bashrc` (if not already there):

```bash
grep -q '/usr/local/go/bin' ~/.bashrc || echo 'export PATH=/usr/local/go/bin:~/.npm-global/bin:$PATH' >> ~/.bashrc
```
